groups.name: Landmark Danish prestige TV dramas (original Danish titles)
groups.explanation: Riget (The Kingdom), Borgen, Broen (The Bridge), and Forbrydelsen (The Killing) are all landmark Danish prestige television dramas. All four are known in their original Danish-language titles and each spawned international remakes or achieved major global export, defining the 'Nordic noir' and Scandinavian drama movements of the 2000s and 2010s.

groups.name: Fictional self-contained community settings in TV
groups.explanation: Stars Hollow (Gilmore Girls), Royston Vasey (The League of Gentlemen), Sunnydale (Buffy the Vampire Slayer), and Wayward Pines (Wayward Pines) are all fictional, insular, self-contained community settings in television — small towns or localities that function as sealed worlds with their own internal logic, cut off (physically or culturally) from the outside.

groups.name: TV characters known for unironic monologues of self-mythology
groups.explanation: Jenna Maroney (30 Rock — constant delusional self-aggrandizement played straight by the character), Dennis Reynolds (It's Always Sunny in Philadelphia — the DENNIS System, 'I am a golden god'), Hannah Horvath (Girls — 'I think I may be the voice of my generation'), and Don Draper (Mad Men — the Carousel pitch, his constructed self-mythology as Dick Whitman reborn) all deliver defining, unironic monologues in which they cast themselves as exceptional, historic, or singular.

groups.name: Things associated with Carmela — not Tony — Soprano
groups.explanation: Rosalie Aprile (Carmela's closest friend, whose orbit is entirely Carmela's — not Tony's world), Livia Soprano (Tony's mother, but specifically Carmela's defining foil and the woman she fears becoming — their relationship is a Carmela storyline), Edie Falco (the actress who played Carmela Soprano, not Tony Gandolfini's character), and Father Intintola (Carmela's parish priest and the object of her near-affair — entirely a Carmela storyline) all point specifically to Carmela Soprano's arc. The trap is that any Sopranos tile reads as 'Tony Soprano' to a casual solver.
